newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer sees cyclical upturn in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer sees cyclical upturn in Germany.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said second-quarter economic data appeared to show a cyclical upturn in the German economy.
Tietmeyer, speaking as chairman of the Group of 10 central bankers, said there were also signs that overall world economic recovery was continuing.
Tietmeyer was speaking after talks among G-10 central bank governors at their monthly meeting at the Basle-based Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
Tietmeyer said recent data from Germany showed a better second quarter. "It seems to be the case that there is a cyclical upturn," he said.
"But one should not overestimate the second quarter figures because to some extent they are influenced by special seasonal factors in the first quarter," he said without elaborating.
Tietmeyer said reports from the G-10 governors showed that the global economy was continuing to recover. Economic recovery in the United States and Canda was continuing as well as in Japan.
The situation was mixed in Europe, with some countries growing faster than others. He said growth was strong in Britain and the Netherlands.
"The Dutch economy is performing well all in all. This is the results and fruits of what they have done in the last four or five years," he said.
Tietmeyer said that in continental Europe it was very important for governments to continue consolidating budgets and reforming social welfare and labour laws in order to promote economic recoveries.
